subject: Creating one legend for different datasets

messages.author: 1842f0e4613ff43b
messages.subject: Creating one legend for different datasets
parts:
Dear all,

I'm struggling with a (possibly) simple question:


library(ggplot2)

a <- data.frame(x = rnorm(100)) ##
b <- data.frame(y = rnorm(50)) ## datasets a and b are unbalanced

ggplot(aes(x = x), data = a) + geom_density() +
geom_density(aes(x = y), data = b, lty = 2)


How can I create one legend that shows my two line types?

Thanks in advance,

Bernd

messages.subject: RE: Creating one legend for different datasets
parts:
Dear Bernard,

The easiest way is to combine (append) both datasets and add an
identifying variable.

dataset <- data.frame(type = c(rep("a", 100), rep("b", 50)), x =
c(rnorm(100), rnorm(50, sd = 0.5)))
ggplot(dataset, aes(x = x, colour = type)) + geom_density()

HTH,

Thierry

If you check out the reshape package (especially 'melt') you'll get the picture that things work better (read more intuitively) with data in the 'vertical' format (and a single data.frame).

ie rather than

a, b
3.4, 5.4

id.var1, value
a, 3.4
b, 5.4

(with an arbitrary number of id.var, of course). That way your unbalance issues aren't important.

If it's truly not possible with your data that would be very interesting and we'd appreciate a minimal example :)

> (So, there is no simple way of creating a completely arbitrary legend in
> ggplot2...)
No.
